headline: Chip Rout Meets Homebuilder Rally as Market Splits Evenly
body_html:
Stocks are running in place at midday on Friday, October 30, with 261 of the 533 names we track higher and 264 lower. The even count hides sharp moves underneath. All prices are intraday and not final.

Semiconductors are the clear pressure point, down 4.82% as a group. AMD is off 10.31%, FormFactor 10.18% and Sandisk 9.92%. Software is softer too, down 0.38%, and Twilio is the session's steepest faller at 23.53%. Homebuilders are the counterweight, up 3.18%. Consumer names gained 0.74% and healthcare 0.28%, while industrials lost 0.62% and materials 0.74%. Capri is the standout winner, up 14.85%, with Cavco Industries up 11.27%.

Into the close, watch whether chip selling steadies or spreads to the wider technology complex. Energy is down 0.32% even though oil is on course for a fourth straight monthly gain after the tanker attack near Hormuz, so the late tone in crude and the Iran diplomacy headlines both matter. Monday, November 2, is the next trading day.

briefs.headline: Capri leads the board with a double-digit jump
briefs.body: Capri Holdings is up 14.85% at midday, the largest gain among the stocks we track. The luxury name is pulling the consumer group to a 0.74% advance. With prices still moving, the question is whether buyers hold the gain into the close.

briefs.headline: Homebuilding names catch a strong bid
briefs.body: Homebuilders are up 3.18%, the best sector reading of the session. Cavco Industries has gained 11.27% and flooring maker Mohawk Industries 5.04%. The strength reaches beyond builders into housing-linked suppliers.

briefs.headline: Twilio, Bright Horizons and Roblox take heavy hits
briefs.body: Twilio has dropped 23.53% and Bright Horizons 20.34%, the two steepest declines in our universe. Roblox is down 11.38%. The losses are stock-specific and far outpace the 0.38% decline in software overall.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors bear the brunt of the selling
briefs.body: The chip group is down 4.82%, far worse than any other sector. AMD has lost 10.31%, equipment maker FormFactor 10.18% and memory name Sandisk 9.92%. Whether the selling eases into the close is a key test for the tape.

briefs.headline: Oil heads for a fourth monthly gain on supply worries
briefs.body: Crude is set to finish October higher for a fourth straight month after a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was reportedly hit by limpet mines. Separately, the US has loaned 40 million barrels from its strategic reserve, the last part of a global agreement. Energy stocks are down 0.32%.

briefs.headline: Iran diplomacy stays in focus
briefs.body: Qatari mediators have returned to Tehran to push for a deal with Washington. President Trump said the conflict should be wrapped up soon, and that Vice President Vance's outreach concerned medical supplies. Traders will watch for any shift in tone before the weekend.
